decisions.reason: It stayed prominently marketed through 2024, is close to the firm's core optical-navigation business, and in a growing industry with organisational slack its likely performance is good enough relative to aspiration to continue.
This product line has clear positive feedback from a high-status ESA mission and strong strategic fit, so its outcomes likely exceed aspiration and strongly favor retention.
It remained on its own page across both years and builds directly on the firm's established sensing capabilities, so management would likely keep it while results continue to mature.

Its weaker website prominence suggests results may be below the firm's preferred aspiration level, but because it is still on the market, close to core capabilities, and the firm has slack, near-term withdrawal is not the most likely choice.

As a newly launched 2024 product line with its own page and strong fit to radiation-hard space imaging needs, it is too early and too strategically aligned for the firm to drop absent clearer underperformance.

This is a newer and more niche product with only limited market signaling so far, but because it builds on existing competences and the firm is innovative and expanding, management would likely allow more time before reallocating resources.
